result.summary: The layout is largely coherent, but there are a few visual defects: a duplicated restaurant card in the 'Fastest near you' carousel, clipped card text with no ellipsis, an inconsistently styled favorite button, and the category chip row and carousel cut abruptly at the right viewport edge.

issues.description: The 'Fastest near you' carousel shows two identical 'Green Bowl Poké' cards with the same image, 15–25 min ETA and €0.90 delivery, which looks like a duplicated data entry or repeated list rendering bug.
issues.suggestion: De-duplicate the restaurant list by unique ID before rendering the carousel, or verify the API isn't returning the same venue twice.

issues.description: The third card in 'Fastest near you' ('Smash Bros Bu...') is hard-clipped at the screen edge and its title is cut mid-word with no ellipsis, making it look broken rather than scrollable.
issues.suggestion: Add consistent horizontal padding/peek for the carousel so the next card is partially but intentionally visible, and apply text-overflow: ellipsis with a fixed card width so titles truncate cleanly.

issues.description: The favorite (heart) buttons on the two 'Popular right now' cards use different treatments: a white circle with dark outline on the ramen card and a dark/translucent circle on the pizza card, so they appear inconsistent.
issues.suggestion: Use one shared favorite-button component with a fixed background and icon colour (or a consistent scrim) regardless of the card image.

issues.description: The category filter chip row is cut off at the right edge with a sliver of an additional chip visible, giving no clear affordance that the row scrolls.
issues.suggestion: Add trailing padding and/or a fade/gradient mask at the edge so the partial chip reads as an intentional scroll hint.

issues.description: The second 'Popular right now' card is truncated by the bottom navigation bar with none of its title or metadata visible, so the section's last item appears incomplete.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom content inset equal to the nav bar height so the final card can scroll fully into view.
